### You pay for capacity your workloads never use

Cast AI sets each workload’s CPU and memory requests from observed usage, then bin-packs pods onto fewer, better-fitting nodes and moves eligible workloads to spot instances. Your node count follows real demand instead of peak requests.

### The GPUs you need aren't available where you run

When your region runs out of GPUs, Cast AI provisions nodes in other clouds and regions through OMNI Compute and schedules eligible workloads there, while your control plane stays in your current cluster. For GPUs you already have, time-slicing and MIG let several workloads share one device.

[Learn about cross-cloud GPUs](https://cast.ai/cross-cloud-gpu-access/)

### Your database is slow and overloaded

Cast AI’s Database Optimizer sits in front of PostgreSQL and MySQL. It caches repeated reads, pools connections so traffic spikes don’t exhaust your connection limit, and flags slow queries with suggested fixes.

[Learn about Database Optimizer](https://cast.ai/database-optimization/)

## Cast AI observes, decides, and acts

It reads how your workloads and nodes behave, works out what should change, and applies eligible changes to live infrastructure within your policies. When a change belongs in your repo, it opens a pull request for your team to review.

Observe and decide

Workload rightsizing informs node capacity, bin-packing, and placement. Node conditions and available capacity inform workload adjustments and remediation. Cast AI connects both while preserving existing policies and integrations.
